tools.name: get_shop_facts
tools.description: What varioroam is and how it works, in the shop’s own words: the configurable eSIM, ranges, delivery, payment, hotspot, activation, top-ups (add data or days), e-mails, support. Use for any question that is not a price.

tools.name: list_destinations
tools.description: Every country varioroam can build an eSIM for, with the number of selectable networks and the starting price (1 GB, 1 day, cheapest network). Use to check coverage or to compare many countries at once.

tools.name: get_networks
tools.description: The mobile networks the customer can tick for one country (operator name, 4G/5G) with the price of a reference eSIM on each network alone (1 GB · 7 days), so you can say which network is the cheapest and what the others add.

tools.name: quote_esim
tools.description: Use while the customer is still deciding — "how much is …?": the exact price of one eSIM configuration (country, data GB 1–100, days 1–90, networks), the server price the customer would pay. Quote it as returned, never compute or scale it yourself. The result carries a buy_url for reference; when th

tools.name: price_grid
tools.description: Prices for several GB × days combinations of one country in one call (max 8 × 8), e.g. to compare with other providers or to find the best fit for a trip. Same server prices as quote_esim.

tools.name: recommend_config
tools.description: Use when the customer describes a trip instead of a size: country (or up to 5), days and how they use data (usage light / normal / heavy, or gb_per_day). Sizes the data pool from the data guide and returns three server-quoted configurations per country — exact, comfortable (×1.5) and generous (×2) —

tools.name: start_checkout
tools.description: Use only once the customer has decided to buy ("I'll take it", "how do I buy?"): the checkout handoff. Returns the buy_url to give the customer, the final price and a ready-to-send checkout block (next_step, payment_methods, delivery) — on the page they press "Get it" and pay securely. No account ne

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: start_checkout · Public sink: start_checkout.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: start_checkout · Public sink: start_checkout

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "plan_trip" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
